# Phycocyanin harmonization process

Following the completion of the `{dataRetrieval}` download process
described previously, the pipeline contains raw WQP data for each
parameter of interest. Before harmonizing each parameter, we run through
a series of universal “pre-harmonization” steps to ensure consistent
column types, site metadata, and time zones across the dataset.

Phycocyanin is a water-soluble phycobiliprotein accessory pigment
characteristic of freshwater cyanobacteria, exhibiting an in-water
absorption maximum near 620 nm and fluorescence emission near 645–650 nm
(Simis et al., 2005; Randolph et al., 2008; Chorus and Welker, 2021).
The sections below walk through the pre-harmonization and harmonization
steps for phycocyanin, explaining how incompatible measurement scales
(mass concentration, relative probe fluorescence, and sensor-estimated
cell density), misfiled accessory pigments, daily statistical summaries,
and analytical methodologies are separated, cleaned, tiered, and
flagged.

## Pre-harmonization of the raw phycocyanin WQP dataset

At the start of the pre-harmonization process the raw phycocyanin WQP
dataset contains 157.2 thousand rows.

<figcaption aria-hidden="true">Bar plot showing the row count update for
the current harmonization step.</figcaption>

### Missing results

Next, rows flagged as truly missing results are dropped based on
`"analysis lost"`, `"not analyzed"`, `"not recorded"`,
`"not collected"`, or `"no measurement taken"` in `ResultCommentText`
when no measurement value is available.

This step removes 1967 rows of data, leaving 155.3 thousand rows
remaining.

<figure>
<img
src="chapters/09_phyco_harmonization_files/figure-gfm/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png"
alt="Bar plot showing the row count update for the current harmonization step." />
<figcaption aria-hidden="true">Bar plot showing the row count update for
the current harmonization step.</figcaption>
</figure>

<br>

### Filter status

The final step in pre-harmonization filters `ResultStatusIdentifier` to
retain only records with status:

- `"Accepted"`
- `"Final"`
- `"Historical"`
- `"Validated"`
- `"Preliminary"`
- `NA`

Records marked `"Provisional"` or other non-finalized statuses are
dropped (766 rows), leaving 154.5 thousand rows remaining.

## Harmonization-ready phycocyanin dataset

Once ready for harmonization, the phycocyanin WQP dataset contains the
following `CharacteristicName`s: Algae-Phycocyanin, Phycocyanin,
Phycocyanin (probe), Phycocyanin (probe relative fluorescence),
Phycocyanins.

<img src="in/phyco/phyco_stacked_char_names.png" alt="Stacked bar chart with counts of phycocyanin CharacteristicName records" width="650"/>

<br>

### Filter media, non-target pigments, and daily summaries; categorize parameters

In this step, we first recover empty `ResultMeasure.MeasureUnitCode`
entries from `DetectionQuantitationLimitMeasure.MeasureUnitCode` when
non-detect rows report their units only in the detection-limit metadata.
We then apply three domain-specific filters before assigning phycocyanin
parameter categories:

1.  **Water media filtering**: `ActivityMediaSubdivisionName` must be
    `"Surface Water"`, `"Water"`, `"Estuary"`, or `NA`, removing
    `"Ocean Water"`.
2.  **Non-target pigment exclusion**: WQP submissions occasionally file
    accessory phycobiliprotein or chlorophyll fluorescence data under
    phycocyanin `CharacteristicName`s. In particular, estuarine probe
    records annotated `"YSI - BGA-PE"` (phycoerythrin) in
    `ResultCommentText` or `ResultAnalyticalMethod.MethodName`, as well
    as USGS parameter codes for phycoerythrin, allophycocyanin, or
    `fChl`, are excluded.
3.  **Daily statistical summary filtering**: Continuous water quality
    sondes frequently archive multiple daily summary statistics at the
    same station and date (`"Minimum"`, `"Maximum"`, `"Delta"`,
    `"Median"`, and `"Mean"`). Including extremes alongside central
    tendencies would collapse spreads into site averages during
    downstream aggregation, so we drop non-central statistical summaries
    while retaining instantaneous (`NA`) and daily `"Mean"` records
    (which are subsequently flagged in `misc_flag`).

Because optical *in vivo* relative fluorescence units (`RFU`/`IVFU`) and
sensor-estimated cell counts (`#/mL`) cannot be converted to phycocyanin
mass concentration (`ug/L`) without empirical, taxon- and
instrument-specific calibrations (Bertone et al., 2018; Foster et al.,
2022), surviving records are separated into three incompatible
`parameter` groups:

<!-- Table created with https://www.tablesgenerator.com/markdown_tables -->

| Parameter | Definition |
|----|----|
| Phycocyanin | Phycocyanin mass concentration records with `ResultMeasure.MeasureUnitCode` in `"ug/l"`, `"ug/L"`, `"mg/m3"`, `"ppb"`, `"mg/l"`, `"mg/L"`, `"ppm"`, `"ug/ml"`, `"ug/mL"`, or `"mg/cm3"` |
| Phycocyanin relative fluorescence | Optical *in vivo* probe relative fluorescence records with units `"RFU"` or `"IVFU"` |
| Phycocyanin cell density | Cyanobacterial cell-density equivalents derived from phycocyanin assays or calibrated sensors with units `"#/mL"`, `"#/ml"`, or `"cells/mL"` |

<br>

Records excluded by the media, non-target pigment, or daily summary
statistic filters are dropped (`n =` 82,840). A summary of excluded
records is shown below:


### Document and remove fails

In this step we filter out records containing failure or
sensor-malfunction language across `ActivityCommentText`,
`ResultLaboratoryCommentText`, `ResultCommentText`,
`ResultDetectionConditionText`, and `ResultMeasureValue_original` (the
character copy of `ResultMeasureValue` prior to numeric coercion).

After auditing phycocyanin-specific WQP comment strings to exclude
benign environmental notes (such as `"DO probe unstable"`, `"warm day"`,
`"broken clouds"`, or unrelated selenium/pH regulatory exceedances), we
match the following case-insensitive phrases: `"beyond accept"`,
`"cancelled"`, `"contaminat"`, `"error"`, `"fail"`, `"improper"`,
`"instrument down"`, `"interference"`, `"invalid"`, `"no result"`,
`"no sample"`, `"no test"`, `"not accept"`, `"outside of accept"`,
`"problem"`, `"questionable"`, `"suspect"`, `"unable"`, `"violation"`,
`"reject"`, `"no data"`, `"value extrapolated"`, `"criteria exceed"`,
`"biased"`, `"parameter not required"`, `"not visited"`,
`"warm sample"`, `"broken bottle"`, `"broken cooler"`,
`"received broken"`, `"broken sensor"`, `"time not documented"`,
`"wiper stopped"`, `"wiper not parked"`, `"sonde out of water"`,
`"sonde stopped recording"`, `"stopped working"`, `"not working"`,
`"off scale"`, and `"censored"`.

Below are pie charts summarizing failure phrase detections for each
column that contained matches (note that detections are not mutually
exclusive):

### Clean MDLs

Method detection limits (MDLs) are cleaned identically to prior
AquaMatch parameters. Where numeric values are `NA`, non-detect
indicators (`"non-detect"`, `"not detect"`, `"non detect"`,
`"undetect"`, `"below"`, `"Present <QL"`, `"ND"`, `"nd"`) trigger
substitution from `DetectionQuantitationLimitMeasure.MeasureValue`, and
`<` numeric qualifiers in `ResultMeasureValue_original` are parsed
directly. Imputed non-detects are drawn uniformly between `0` and
`0.5 * MDL`, while preserving units from
`DetectionQuantitationLimitMeasure.MeasureUnitCode` when
`ResultMeasure.MeasureUnitCode` is blank.

The `mdl_flag` column records `0` (unadjusted at/above MDL), `1`
(imputed using EPA `0` to `0.5 * MDL`), or `2` (reported numeric value
below MDL, unadjusted).

This step drops 0 rows, leaving 71.1 thousand remaining.

<img
src="chapters/09_phyco_harmonization_files/figure-gfm/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png"
alt="Bar plot showing the row count update for the current harmonization step." />
<figcaption aria-hidden="true">Bar plot showing the row count update for
the current harmonization step.</figcaption>
</figure>

<br>

### Clean approximate values

Records with missing numeric `ResultMeasureValue` that contain numeric
text and approximation phrases (`"result approx"`, `"RESULT IS APPROX"`,
`"value approx"`) are cleaned and flagged (`approx_flag = 1`), while
unadjusted rows receive `approx_flag = 0`.

This step drops 0 rows, leaving 71.1 thousand rows remaining.

<figure>
<img
src="chapters/09_phyco_harmonization_files/figure-gfm/unnamed-chunk-17-1.png"
alt="Bar plot showing the row count update for the current harmonization step." />
<figcaption aria-hidden="true">Bar plot showing the row count update for
the current harmonization step.</figcaption>
</figure>

<br>

### Clean values with “greater than” data

Similarly, unadjusted records containing `>` qualifiers and numeric text
are parsed by stripping `>`, `=`, and `*` characters
(`greater_flag = 1`), leaving all other records with `greater_flag = 0`.

0 rows are removed, leaving 71.1 thousand rows remaining.

<figure>
<img
src="chapters/09_phyco_harmonization_files/figure-gfm/unnamed-chunk-19-1.png"
alt="Bar plot showing the row count update for the current harmonization step." />
<figcaption aria-hidden="true">Bar plot showing the row count update for
the current harmonization step.</figcaption>
</figure>

<br>

### Drop unresolved NA and negative measurements

Following non-detect, approximate, and greater-than recovery, remaining
unresolved `NA`/`NaN` values and negative measurements
(`harmonized_value < 0`, which occur primarily as zero-offset baseline
drift on continuous optical sondes) are removed because neither pigment
concentrations, positive relative fluorescence, nor cell counts can be
physically negative.

4224 rows are removed, leaving 66.9 thousand rows remaining.

alt="Bar plot showing the row count update for the current harmonization step." />

the current harmonization step.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Clean depth data

The four WQP depth columns are standardized to meters and summarized via
`depth_flag` as documented in the *Tiering, flagging, and quality
control philosophy* chapter (`0` = no depth, `1` = discrete depth, `2` =
integrated top/bottom depths, `3` = both discrete and integrated depths
present).

0 rows are removed, leaving 66.9 thousand rows remaining.

### Filter and tier methods

In preparation for tiering, clearly misassigned non-phycocyanin
laboratory methods (e.g., Standard Methods `4500-P B` phosphorus sample
preparation) are filtered out. Remaining records are assigned to three
analytical method tiers reflecting cross-provider comparability and
vulnerability to optical matrix artifacts:

<br>

<!-- Table created with https://www.tablesgenerator.com/markdown_tables -->

| Tier | Name | Description | Phycocyanin Details |
|----|----|----|----|
| 0 | Restrictive | Data that are verifiably self-similar across organizations and time-periods and can be considered highly reliable | Laboratory extractive benchtop fluorometry, spectrophotometry, and HPLC (`ug/L`; e.g., USGS p-code `52905` / `SP012` / `FL083`, `MNPCA` modified Otsuki et al. (1994), `MDEQ_WQ_WQX` HPLC). Cell lysis extracts pigment into solution, eliminating *in vivo* cellular packaging, light history/quenching, and temperature effects (Horváth et al., 2013; Kasinak et al., 2015). |
| 1 | Narrowed | Data with documented instrumentation/SOPs that may exhibit matrix-dependent bias across deployments | Documented *in situ* optical fluorometric probes/sondes (`YSI EXO`, `YSI 6131`, `Multiparameter Water Quality Sonde`, USGS p-codes `32319`, `32321`, `32329`, `32335`, `95201`–`95204`) and documented optical lab fluorometry/spectrometry lacking explicit extraction confirmation. Subject to inverse temperature quenching (~1% per deg C; Watras et al., 2017), turbidity attenuation, and FDOM/chlorophyll-*a* spectral cross-talk (Zamyadi et al., 2012; Bertone et al., 2018; Foster et al., 2022). |
| 2 | Inclusive | Records with missing, generic (`LOCAL`, `Unknown`), or misapplied method metadata | Unspecified methods (`NA`), adapted chlorophyll-*a* method identifiers (`445.0` on phycocyanin probes), or unverified probe entries without instrument/SOP metadata. |

<br>

combination of `CharacteristicName`, analytical method, USGS p-code,
unit, and sample fraction maps onto Tiers 0–2:

### Flag based on field methods

Next, `field_flag` cross-checks whether sample collection metadata
(`ActivityTypeCode`, `SampleCollectionMethod.MethodName`,
`SampleCollectionEquipmentName`) and `ResultSampleFractionText` agree
with the assigned analytical tier:

- `field_flag = 0` (**Reasonable**): Extractive lab Tier 0 records
  collected with discrete water-sampling gear (`grab`, `bottle`,
  `kemmerer`, `van dorn`, `filter`, `Sample-Routine`), or documented
  optical Tier 1 sonde records with explicit field/sensor metadata
  (`Field Msr/Obs`, `Probe/Sensor`, `Sonde`) and non-dissolved fraction.
- `field_flag = 1` (**Suspect**): Tier 0 records reporting
  sensor/field-only collection, or Tier 1 optical probe records
  reporting `"Dissolved"` sample fraction or bottle/grab sampling
  without documented *in situ* sensor deployment.
- `field_flag = 2` (**Inconclusive**): Tier 2 records or Tier 0/1
  records where sample collection metadata are `"Unknown"` or `NA`.

No records are dropped in this step (0 rows dropped), leaving 66.9
thousand rows remaining.

### Miscellaneous flag

For phycocyanin, `misc_flag` identifies two distinct data conditions
that are held out from simultaneous replicate averaging during
aggregation so end users can filter them explicitly:

- `misc_flag = 0`: Instantaneous/discrete observations within standard
  surface-water calibration bounds.
- `misc_flag = 1`: Continuous sonde daily `"Mean"` summary rows
  (`StatisticalBaseCode == "Mean"`), distinguishing multi-hour temporal
  averages from instantaneous point observations.
- `misc_flag = 2`: Extreme bloom/scum concentrations exceeding standard
  linear optical calibration bounds (`> 2,000 ug/L`, `> 100 RFU` or
  `IVFU`, or `> 280,000 #/mL`; Bertone et al., 2018; Foster et al.,
  2022; Chorus and Welker, 2021). Note that records exceeding both
  criteria receive `misc_flag = 2`.

| **Parameter** | **Units** | **Flag = 1** | **Flag = 2** |
|----|----|----|----|
| Phycocyanin | ug/L | `StatisticalBaseCode == "Mean"` | `> 2,000 ug/L` |
| Phycocyanin relative fluorescence | RFU, IVFU | `StatisticalBaseCode == "Mean"` | `> 100 RFU` or `> 100 IVFU` |
| Phycocyanin cell density | \#/mL | `StatisticalBaseCode == "Mean"` | `> 280,000 #/mL` |

### Remove unrealistic values

Prior to finalizing the dataset, we remove physically impossible
bulk-water phycocyanin mass values above `100,000 ug/L` (`100 mg/L` pure
phycocyanin protein; reflecting sensor cell-density entries misfiled
under `ug/L`) while retaining verified dissolved bloom/scum extracts up
to `41,000 ug/L` under `misc_flag = 2`. We also remove any sampling
depths `> 592 m`, the maximum lake depth in the United States (Larson,
1972).

8 rows are removed, leaving 66.9 thousand rows remaining.

### Aggregate simultaneous records

The final step of phycocyanin harmonization aggregates simultaneous
observations (matching across the 26 grouping columns `parameter`,
`OrganizationIdentifier`, `MonitoringLocationIdentifier`,
`MonitoringLocationTypeName`, `ResolvedMonitoringLocationTypeName`,
`ActivityStartDate`, `ActivityStartTime.Time`,
`ActivityStartTime.TimeZoneCode`, `harmonized_tz`,
`harmonized_local_time`, `harmonized_utc`, `ActivityStartDateTime`,
`harmonized_top_depth_value`, `harmonized_top_depth_unit`,
`harmonized_bottom_depth_value`, `harmonized_bottom_depth_unit`,
`harmonized_discrete_depth_value`, `harmonized_discrete_depth_unit`,
`depth_flag`, `mdl_flag`, `approx_flag`, `greater_flag`, `tier`,
`field_flag`, `misc_flag`, and `harmonized_units`) into mean values
(`harmonized_value`), replicate counts (`harmonized_row_count`), and
coefficients of variation (`harmonized_value_cv`), tagged by
`subgroup_id` for back-joining with `p3_phyco_preagg_grouped`.

As with CDOM, records with `misc_flag` equal to `1` (daily means) or `2`
(extreme bloom/scum values exceeding calibration ceilings) are held out
from grouping and re-appended with `NA` in `subgroup_id`,
`harmonized_row_count`, and `harmonized_value_cv`.

3760 rows are aggregated away, leaving 63.1 thousand rows remaining in
the final harmonized phycocyanin dataset.
